title_prefix: Every removal invalidates the whole mini
mechanism: The code reading is exactly right on the current tree. TXGRAPH has no incremental mining index: CHUNK-INDEX (src/mempool/txgraph.lisp:153) is a cached simple-vector, %CLUSTER-UPDATED clears it at src/mempool/txgraph.lisp:281 and TXGRAPH-REMOVE-TRANSACTION clears it at src/mempool/txgraph.lisp:388, and %ENSURE-CHUNK-INDEX (src/mempool/txgraph.lisp:310-323) rebuilds it by walking every cluster in the graph, collecting every chunk and SORTing the whole vector with %COMPARE-MAIN. %CLUSTER-UPDATED is reached from every mutation path (add txgraph.lisp:341, split 353/364, dependency merge 480/523, set-fee 559), so add, remove, add-dependency and even a set-fee to the SAME value all invalidate the whole global index -- verified in the image with a positive control (index T after each %ENSURE-CHUNK-INDEX, NIL after each mutation): (:AFTER-INDEX T :AFTER-ADD NIL :AFTER-INDEX2 T :AFTER-REMOVE NIL :AFTER-INDEX3 T :AFTER-SAME-FEE-SET NIL :AFTER-INDEX4 T :AFTER-DEP NIL). Core keeps m_main_chunkindex as a std::set<ChunkData, ChunkOrder> (refs/bitcoin/src/txgraph.cpp:535-547) maintained incrementally by ClearChunkData/CreateChunkData (txgraph.cpp:881-900), one node extracted and one re-inserted per changed chunk, and GetWorstMainChunk (txgraph.cpp:3258-3282) reads m_main_chunkindex.rbegin() with no rebuild, so Core's TrimToSize loop (refs/bitcoin/src/txmempool.cpp:861-911) costs O(log n) per evicted chunk. Ours: MEMPOOL-TRIM-TO-SIZE (src/mempool/mempool.lisp:1726-1767) alternates TXGRAPH-GET-WORST-MAIN-CHUNK (txgraph.lisp:812-824, calls %ENSURE-CHUNK-INDEX) with MEMPOOL-REMOVE, so each evicted CHUNK pays one full sort of the entire pool. MAKE-BLOCK-BUILDER (txgraph.lisp:844-851) pays one too. Refuter checks: (1) the trim is NOT unconditional -- MEMPOOL-ADD gates it on (> (mempool-dynamic-usage mempool) (mempool-max-size mempool)) at mempool.lisp:1019-1022, exactly Core's effective behaviour, so the defect needs a FULL pool and does not fire on an under-cap node; (2) the node lock IS held across the whole trim -- HANDLE-TX wraps the entire accept in WITH-CURRENT-NODE-LOCK (src/networking/protocol.lisp:1839; the macro is a bt recursive lock on (bl:node-lock bl:*node*), protocol.lisp:7-19) on the sync thread (src/networking/peer.lisp:149), and the same lock is taken by block acceptance (src/networking/ibd.lisp:3631 ACCEPT-BLOCK-BODY, 3719, 3819, 4033), the mining assembler (src/mining/assembler.lisp:176) and every RPC/wallet handler (bl.rpc:with-node-lock).
consequence: S1 confirmed on the stated bar: at DEFAULT -maxmempool (300 MB) a full pool makes the node unable to keep up. Per-entry modelled usage measured through the real mempool: 960 B for a 141-vB 1-in/2-out P2WPKH entry (-> 312,498 entries at the cap) and 816 B for a 189-vB P2PKH entry (-> 367,645), so the finding's 'several hundred thousand entries' is right. Filled to exactly 300,000,016 bytes of modelled usage (312,500 entries) and set the cap there, EVERY subsequent MEMPOOL-ADD costs 0.719 s (10 accepts, 0.667-0.790 s each, pool count constant at 312,500 -- one in, one out). Isolation at that size: the chunk-index rebuild alone is 0.644 s, an add with :DEFER-TRIM T (no trim, no rebuild) is 0.000 s, a full add is 0.667 s -- the whole per-accept cost IS the rebuild, and the whole rebuild IS the sort (collect 0.002 s, sort 0.644 s). That caps the node at ~1.4 accepted tx/s while holding the node lock; mainnet confirms ~4,000 tx per block (~6.7 tx/s) so a full pool cannot even keep pace with the confirmation rate, and at a mere 1 accepted tx/s the node lock is held 72% of wall time, so block connection, compact-block reconstruction, mining and RPC all stall behind tx acceptance. getblocktemplate pays the same rebuild after any mutation (measured 0.119 s at 100k, i.e. ~0.6 s at the cap). Honest scope limits: the pool must be at the cap (a lightly-used or testnet node never pays this); a heavily chained pool has ~8x fewer chunks and pays ~10x less (0.030 s/eviction at 200k txs in chains of 20 vs 0.309 s for singletons), but real mempools are singleton-dominated and the full-pool measurement above used a realistic singleton shape; and correctness is NOT affected -- the rebuilt order equals an incrementally maintained one, which is what the %ENSURE-CHUNK-INDEX docstring means by 'unobservable'. That docstring is true of the OUTPUT and false of the COST.
evidence: All probes run in the project container (bitcoin-lisp-sbcl:2.6.5-4, SBCL 2.6.5, warm image) with bitcoin-lisp.mempool::*txgraph-shadow-checks* bound to NIL; the daemon was shared with other agents' containers, so absolute times are if anything pessimistic for the container, not for the finding. TXGRAPH-level, independent singletons, one eviction = TXGRAPH-GET-WORST-MAIN-CHUNK + TXGRAPH-REMOVE-TRANSACTION: 20,000 txs (:FIRST-INDEX-SECS 0.013 :CACHED-LOOKUP-SECS 0.0 :SECS-PER-EVICTION 0.0106); 50,000 (:FIRST-INDEX-SECS 0.068 :SECS-PER-EVICTION 0.0414); 200,000 (:FIRST-INDEX-SECS 0.392 :SECS-PER-EVICTION 0.3088, collect 0.002 s / sort 0.730 s). Chained shape (chains of 20): 20,000 txs -> 3,985 chunks, 0.0019 s/eviction; 200,000 txs -> 39,832 chunks, 0.0304 s/eviction. Real mempool shape: (:TXS 5000 :USAGE 4080016 :USAGE-PER-TX 816.0 :VSIZE-PER-TX 189.0 :ENTRIES-AT-300MB 367645) and (:TXS 5000 :USAGE 4800016 :USAGE-PER-TX 960.0 :VSIZE-PER-TX 141.0 :ENTRIES-AT-300MB 312498). Full-pool steady state (cap set to current usage, then ordinary MEMPOOL-ADD calls, no defer-trim): 30,000 entries 0.0316 s/accept; 100,000 0.1457 s; 200,000 0.4356 s; 312,500 (:USAGE 300000016 :CAP 300000016 :FINAL-COUNT 312500 :SECS-PER-ACCEPT 0.7187, per-accept 0.667..0.790). Isolation at 312,500: (:REBUILD-SECS 0.644 :PARTS (:CHUNKS 312500 :COLLECT-SECS 0.002 :SORT-SECS 0.644) :ADD-DEFER-TRIM-SECS 0.0 :ADD-FULL-SECS 0.667). MAKE-BLOCK-BUILDER at 100,000: 0.119 s. Invalidation control (positive control included): (:AFTER-INDEX T :AFTER-ADD NIL :AFTER-INDEX2 T :AFTER-REMOVE NIL :AFTER-INDEX3 T :AFTER-SAME-FEE-SET NIL :AFTER-INDEX4 T :AFTER-DEP NIL). Files: src/mempool/txgraph.lisp:153,229-281,310-323,341,353,364,388,480,523,559,812-824,844-851; src/mempool/mempool.lisp:187-199,416-435,1019-1022,1726-1767; src/networking/protocol.lisp:7-19,1839; src/networking/peer.lisp:149; src/networking/ibd.lisp:3631; src/mining/assembler.lisp:176; refs/bitcoin/src/txgraph.cpp:535-547,881-900,3258-3282; refs/bitcoin/src/txmempool.cpp:861-911. Deviation from the finding's numbers: at 200,000 txgraph-level singletons I measured 0.309 s/eviction where the finding reported 0.1875 s -- same mechanism, my container was busier; every other figure reproduced within noise, and the finding's 200k figure understates the cost.
fix_shape: Port Core's incremental index (do not implement here). Replace the cached CHUNK-INDEX simple-vector with an ordered container holding one node per chunk keyed by %COMPARE-MAIN -- a balanced tree or skiplist over %CHUNK, or an order-statistic structure -- plus a back-pointer from each cluster (or from each chunk-end handle, Core's Entry::m_main_chunkindex_iterator) to its node. Give %CLUSTER-UPDATED the ClearChunkData/CreateChunkData pair (refs/bitcoin/src/txgraph.cpp:881-900): before relinearizing a cluster, extract that cluster's existing chunk nodes; after recomputing its chunks, insert the new ones, so the cost is O(k log C) in the k chunks of the ONE cluster that changed rather than O(C log C) over the whole pool; TXGRAPH-REMOVE-TRANSACTION then extracts only the affected cluster's nodes via %SPLIT-CLUSTER instead of setting the index to NIL. TXGRAPH-GET-WORST-MAIN-CHUNK becomes a read of the last element (Core's m_main_chunkindex.rbegin(), txgraph.cpp:3258-3266) with no rebuild, and MAKE-BLOCK-BUILDER iterates the live container forward -- the existing TXGRAPH-BUILDER-COUNT already models Core's m_main_chunkindex_observers and forbids mutation while a builder exists, so no snapshot copy is needed. Keep the present full rebuild as an equivalence oracle inside TXGRAPH-SANITY-CHECK (it already walks the index at txgraph.lisp:1123-1131) so the incremental structure is checked against the from-scratch sort in the test suite, and cover it with a test that fails on a per-eviction cost that scales with pool size.
